title: Graduate Program — Faculty Resources
text:
Some funding sources do not allow for paying tuitions. In such a case, a faculty member may ask the graduate committee to cover tuition using ARD funding.
Graduate students who receive an annual salary above $19,617 automatically receive a tuition waiver for 12 credit hours per semester (Spring, Summer, and Fall). Since all offers we make to students exceed this threshold, tuition waivers are effectively guaranteed for our funded students.
If a student takes more than 12 credit hours in a semester, tuition applies to the excess hours. If you have an agreement with the graduate committee to cover a student’s tuition, ARD (Agricultural Research Division) will cover those excess credit hour costs.



ARD covers tuition for excess credit hours up to these annual limits. Costs beyond the cap must be covered by other funding sources (you are responsible).








Residency Status
ARD Coverage Cap (per academic year)
Tuition per Credit Hour
Max Excess Hours Covered




Nebraska Resident

~9.6 hrs

~9.4 hrs









Communicate Credit Hour Limits to Your Students



Both resident and non-resident students can take roughly 9 excess credit hours per year before hitting the ARD cap. Costs beyond the cap fall to other funding sources. Please discuss this with your students and encourage them to avoid overloading their schedule in any single semester.





The caps above are adjusted based on the annual salary offered to the student. The baseline salary is $27,000. If the offered salary exceeds this baseline, the difference is subtracted from the cap.
Formula: Adjusted Cap = max(0, Base Cap − (Offered Salary − $27,000))

Example adjusted caps by offered salary.


Offered Salary
Resident Cap
Non-Resident Cap




$27,000 (baseline)
$3,500
$10,000


$30,000
$500
$7,000


$33,000
$0
$4,000









Communicate the Adjusted Cap to Your Students



Make sure your student knows their actual adjusted cap, not just the base cap. If you are offering a salary above $27,000, the tuition coverage available through ARD is reduced accordingly. Students should plan their course loads with their specific cap in mind to avoid unexpected tuition costs.

title: Offer Letter Request
text:
Use the form below (or the button) to submit an offer letter request for a new or existing graduate student. The form will notify the Graduate Program Coordinator and relevant staff once submitted.
Submit Offer Letter Request

title: Offer Letter Request
text:
What to Prepare
Before filling out the form, have the following information ready:

Student name — full legal name for new admits, or select from the dropdown for existing students
Degree program — MS or PhD
Funding sources and cost objects — one per line, separated by |
Annual salary / stipend amount
Funding breakdown by cost object
Funding start and end dates
Years of secured funding
Funding plan beyond the secured period (new students only, if fewer than 4 years secured)

title: Offer Letter Request
text:
After Submission
Once the form is submitted:

An email summary is sent to the Graduate Program Coordinator and staff.
The offer letter is generated and shared with you.

For questions, contact the Graduate Committee Chair at tmieno2@nebraska.edu.

title: ARD Funding decision policy
text: The graduate committee is responsible for allocating departmental funding to graduate students each academic year. This document outlines the criteria and process used to make funding decisions.

title: ARD Funding decision policy
text:
Decision process

The graduate committee distributes a survey to all faculty asking them to indicate funding needs for each of their current students. Any requests that were submitted later than the deadline will be placed at the bottom of priority.
The committee removes ineligible requests (see Eligibility above) and determines whether the available ARD funding is sufficient to cover all remaining requests.
If funding is insufficient, requests are ranked according to the allocation criteria above and funded in priority order until the budget is exhausted.
If ARD funds remain after covering all eligible requests, the committee makes offers to the current pool of incoming applicants within the available budget.

    B --> C{Is ARD funding sufficient<br/>to cover all requests?}
    C -- Yes --> D[Fund all eligible requests]

    E --> F[Fund requests in priority<br/>order until budget is exhausted]
    D --> G{Are ARD funds<br/>remaining?}

title: ARD Funding decision policy
text:
Earning an ARD credit
Sometimes, you cannot identify an applicant who fits well with your research interest even though you have funding to cover a graduate student. If the founder of your project allows for it, you can pay for the current graduate student supported by ARD and earn 1 year GRA credit. You can use that credit to pay for a year of 1 GRA when you need it. This is only when the student will not work for your project (pure monetary swapping).

title: ARD Funding decision policy
section: Expectation for bridge funding when bringing a new student to the program
text:
Expectation for bridge funding when bringing a new student to the program








Years of funding secured
ARD bridge funding provided
Permitted to recruit a new student




1 year
None
No


2 years
Up to 2 years
No


3 years
1 year
Yes


4 years
Possible additional year
Yes




1 year of funding secured
If you have only one year of funding guaranteed and enroll a student, the department will  NOT  provide ARD funding for the remainder of his/her program under any circumstances. Faculty may not recruit graduate students with the expectation that the department will assume long-term financial responsibility for their support. As an alternative, you may identify a current student in need of funding to work for you, or arrange for a student currently supported by ARD to be covered by your funding, thereby earning an ARD credit to apply toward future departmental support for your student.


2 years of funding secured
If you have two years of funding guaranteed for an incoming student, the department will provide bridge funding for up to 2 years. However, you will  NOT  be permitted to recruit any additional new students using your own funding, as those resources should be directed toward supporting your current student.


3 years of funding secured
If you have three years of funding guaranteed for an incoming student, the department is most likely able to provide bridge funding for 1 year as such a student is a top priority as shown below in the table. You are permitted to recruit a new student using your own funding, as you will have provided the student sufficient financial support.


4 years of funding secured
If you have four years of funding guaranteed for an incoming student, the student is in a strong position to receive an additional year of ARD funding if necessary. You are permitted to recruit a new student using your own funding.

title: ARD Funding decision policy
text:
Allocation criteria
The graduate committee uses the following criteria when allocating fellowships. These are considered holistically.

History of funding sources: Students who have received fewer years of ARD funding are given higher priority. The chart below illustrates example funding histories the committee considers.

Academic and research performance: Evidence of progress includes completed coursework, publications, conference presentations, and advisor evaluations.
Advisor co-funding: Students whose advisors contribute partial funding (e.g., from grants) may receive higher priority for departmental support to complete their package.
